title: Thermal proteome profiling of phosphorylated proteoforms
projectDescription: We combined thermal proteome profiling (TPP) with phosphopeptide enrichment to study the thermostability of phosphorylated proteoforms.
sampleProcessingProtocol: After heating, lysing and extraction of remaining soluble protein fraction (with a modified thermal proteome profiling protocol - Savitski et al., Science (2014), samples were processed with a modified SP3 protocol, digested using trypsin and labeled with TMT. Some samples were phosphopeptide-enriched with a Fe3+-IMAC column (similarly to Potel et al., Nature Methods (2018)). Shotgun proteomics using a Lumos Orbitrap was then performed.
dataProcessingProtocol: TMT quantification was used, by using the isobarquant python package (Franken et al., Nat Protoc (2015)), and Mascot 2.4 was used for protein identification. Search parameters: trypsin, missed cleavages 3, peptide tolerance 10ppm, 0.02Da for MS/MS tolerance. Fixed modifications were carbamidomethyl on cysteines and TMT10plex on lysine. Variable modifications included acetylation on protein N-terminus, oxidation of methionine and TMT10plex on peptide N-termini (phosphorylation on STY for phosphoenriched samples). The R programming language was used to analyze the output data.

references.referenceLine: Potel CM, Kurzawa N, Becher I, Typas A, Mateus A, Savitski MM. Impact of phosphorylation on thermal stability of proteins. Nat Methods. 2021
